pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The pathogen, Alternaria dauci, is seedborne and survives on and is spread with carrot seed.

type_of_disease.quote: Carrot leaf blights are caused by two fungal pathogens, Alternaria dauci and Cercospora carotae

affected_parts.quote: A. dauci causes leaf spot and blight... A. dauci occurs on the seed as spores and within the seed as dormant mycelium and/or spores... Initially, infection may occur on the petioles as shallow, black lesions which later spread into the crown and down the root.

summary.value: Foliar symptoms first appear along leaflet margins (and on older/lower leaves) as greenish-brown, water-soaked lesions which enlarge, turn brown to black, and often develop a yellow halo or margin; under favorable conditions lesions coalesce giving leaves a scorched/blighted appearance, and when about 40% of a leaf is infected it yellows, collapses, and dies.
summary.quote: Foliar symptoms of A. dauci first appear along leaflet margins as greenish-brown, water-soaked lesions which enlarge, turn brown to black, and often develop a yellow halo. Older leaves are more susceptible to infection. When about 40% of the leaf is infected, the leaf yellows, collapses, and dies.

diagnostic_features.value: Greenish-brown, water-soaked lesions beginning along leaflet margins and on older/lower leaves that turn brown to black with a yellow halo; common, elongate petiole lesions that can quickly girdle and kill entire leaves; at advanced stages leaves have a scorched appearance and weakened tops break during mechanical harvest.
diagnostic_features.quote: first appear along leaflet margins as greenish-brown, water-soaked lesions which enlarge, turn brown to black, and often develop a yellow halo... Petiole lesions are common, elongate, and can quickly kill entire leaves.

value: Cercospora leaf blight
Bacterial leaf blight
look_alikes.quote: Compared to Cercospora leaf blight, the lesions of Alternaria dauci are more evident initially on the lower, older leaves

value: Plant Alternaria-indexed / certified pathogen-free seed and treat seed with a hot water dip (122Â°F / 50Â°C for 20-25 minutes) or fungicide
Practice rotations out of carrots (2-year minimum; 3-4 years recommended) and avoid continuous carrot culture
Turn under / promptly incorporate carrot residue by tillage or plowing to hasten decomposition of debris and reduce inoculum
Do not plant new fields near existing fields with blight symptoms
Use resistant/tolerant cultivars (e.g. Bolero, Carson, Ithaca, Calgary, Waltham-Hi-Color, Orlando Gold, Hi-Color 9)
Reduce leaf wetness and soil moisture (wider row spacing, break compacted layers, raised ridges, furrow irrigation) and keep carrots vigorously growing and free from injury
Apply first fungicide spray at ~25% disease incidence threshold and continue based on severity/weather, using spray forecast models (e.g. Tom-Cast) and alternating fungicide chemistries

Foliar fungicides/biologicals: azoxystrobin (Quadris), chlorothalonil (Bravo Weather Stik), iprodione (Rovral 4F), pyraclostrobin (Cabrio EG), pyraclostrobin/fluxapyroxad (Merivon), trifloxystrobin (Flint Extra), penthiopyrad (Fontelis), boscalid (Endura), polyoxin D zinc salt (Ph-D), Bacillus subtilis / Serenade ASO (organic-acceptable)
treatments.quote: Planting Alternaria -indexed seed or treating seed in a hot water dip is very important. Turn under carrot residue by tillage or plowing to hasten decomposition of debris ... Practice 2-year rotations and avoid continuous carrot culture. ... apply fungicides when the first blight symptoms appear, at biweekly intervals

conflicts.canonical_value: Apply first fungicide at 25% disease incidence threshold
conflicts.alternative_value: Apply fungicides when the first blight symptoms appear, at biweekly intervals
conflicts.note: UMass and Cornell cite a 25% disease incidence threshold; UC IPM recommends spraying at first symptom onset on biweekly intervals.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The fungus, Alternaria radicina (formerly Stemphylium radicinum ), can be seedborne or may overwinter in crop refuse.

type_of_disease.quote: The fungus, Alternaria radicina (formerly Stemphylium radicinum )

value: Root
Seed
Foliar
Vascular
Stem
affected_parts.quote: necrosis of roots and crowns, foliar blight, seed/umbel blight, and storage rot... lesions on petioles can extend to the vascular system and cause yellowing, wilting, and plant death.

summary.value: Causes seed decay, damping-off, blackened hypocotyls and deformed roots; small to extensive black lesions develop on the root surface with a well-defined border between infected and healthy tissue, and a dry, mealy, black decay develops on roots held in storage. Foliar symptoms are less severe than those of A. dauci.
summary.quote: A. radicina causes seed decay, damping-off, blackened hypocotyls, and deformed roots. A dry, mealy, black decay may develop when carrot roots are held in storage. Foliar symptoms caused by A. radicina are less severe than those caused by A. dauci

diagnostic_features.value: Black lesions on the root surface with a well-defined border between infected and healthy tissues that may not penetrate deeply and enlarge slowly even near freezing; dry, mealy, black storage decay; blackened hypocotyls and deformed roots; petiole lesions extending to the vascular system causing yellowing, wilting, and plant death.
diagnostic_features.quote: black lesions on the root surface, with a well-defined border between infected and healthy tissues. Such lesions may not penetrate deeply. Lesions may enlarge slowly in colder temperatures, even those near freezing.

value: Alternaria Leaf Blight (Alternaria dauci)
look_alikes.quote: Under certain environmental conditions, A. radicina can cause a foliar blight similar to the Alternaria leaf blight incited by A. dauci.

Eradicate A. radicina from seed with a hot water treatment (122Â°F for 30 min)

Plow under / promptly incorporate crop debris soon after harvest
Irrigate so that carrots are dry by nightfall
Plant tolerant cultivars (e.g. Improved Half Long Chantenay, K-2043)

Fungicides: Rovral / iprodione (e.g. Rovral 4 Flowable, Iprodione 4L AG, Meteor), copper products (Bordeaux 6-6-100, C-O-C-S WDG), mancozeb products (Dithane F45 Rainshield, Roper DF Rainshield), Nevado 4F seed treatment (WA/ID only)
treatments.quote: Use pathogen-free seed. Irrigate so that carrots are dry by nightfall. Rotation out of carrots for at least 1 year is important because refuse is the main way the organisms overwinter. Plow under crop debris soon after harvest.
